title: Update on my crypto trend system: I applied your criticism (survivorship-free universe, cold start, monthly walk-forward) and the numbers dropped… but now they're honest. Plus tests on stocks, gold and indices. Looking for ideas.
author: lks777
selftext:
Hi again. A few days ago I posted my system (daily DI + Supertrend, bot on demo on BingX perps). You gave great criticism and I tested all of it. Here's what changed, what worked, what failed, and where I need ideas.



Same as before: everything in R (1R = risk per trade). "Ratio" = total profit ÷ max drawdown. I ALWAYS split into training and exam periods, with rules fixed before looking at the exam. I compare against random controls where it applies.



1. What changed because of your criticism

a) Survivorship-free universe. Instead of my 7 hand-picked coins: each month, the 10 coins with the highest 30-day volume, including ones that later died (LUNA, FTT…). The ratio dropped from 41.7 (my 7 coins) to 10.0, and to 2.6 since 2022. The 41.7 was optimistic, as I suspected.



b) Cold start. I picked the portfolio using only 2018–21 data, froze it, and ran it untouched from 2022 to today. It ended below the core alone (DI + Supertrend) and only slightly above the S&P 500. Picking by looking at the past doesn't work.



c) Automatic monthly review (walk-forward). I have 26 candidate strategies: EMA crosses, channels, EWO, 20-day breakouts, an EMA "fan", and wave-3 starts. Each month, using trades already closed in the previous 36 months, I pick those with ratio ≥ 2, profitable in both 18-month halves, and ≥ 10 trades. At most 6, traded at 0.25× the core risk.



Full system: 2019–22 ratio 9.2 · 2023 → Oct 2026 ratio 4.5 (core alone: 2.8 in 2023–26).

Live on the demo bot. I checked that all 26 candidates produce exactly the same trades in the bot as in the backtest.

2. What worked

"Start of wave 3" on 4h (one of the few measurable things I got out of Elliott): after a valid 1-2 (higher low, 38–79 % retracement), buy on a close above the end of wave 1, only with the daily DI in favour. Stop below wave 2. Random control: 0 of 10 match it.

Better exit (4h DI until +2R, then trail the ZigZag higher lows) + adding a second position on a new signal in the same coin: exam 8.2 → 10.9. All 12 nearby variants also improve.

Bigger size after losing streaks: after 2+ consecutive losses in the same coin, the next trade earns more on average (+0.30R vs −0.06R after a winner; sideways markets chain losses and the next trade is often the real breakout).

With 2× after 2 losses: 9.2 / 4.5 → 11.1 / 6.2. The same number of trades at 2× chosen at random: 9.5 / 4.4.

But 58 % of trades end up at 2× and the drawdown in R rises 55 %. Pure martingale (2× per loss) triples the drawdown.

Stocks: my stock system (long while the weekly DI is bullish, stop at yesterday's low) gives ratio 9.4 (2008–15) / 10.2 (2016–26) on a fixed list of 55 (25 ETFs + 30 large caps). What matters most in stocks is exiting on the weekly DI, not the daily one as in crypto. With the same monthly review: 10.2 → 11.7.

Gold and Nasdaq long, daily (futures since 2000): gold with DI 14 and weekly exit, training 43.2 → exam 6.4 (few trades). Nasdaq exam 9.6. Added to the crypto system: 9.2 / 4.5 → 9.6 / 5.2.

3. What did NOT work (another batch)

"Self-training" drawdown by drawdown: I replayed history; at each drawdown I analysed it and adopted whichever idea would have done best. Worse than doing nothing (12.0 → 9.2), though better than adopting ideas at random (2.2). What you learn mid-drawdown costs profit later and doesn't prevent the next one.

11 "trend is over" filters (weekly DI against, below the 200-day MA, bearish structure, BTC bearish, breadth…). Trades against the higher timeframe WIN: they are the first ones of each new trend.

Waiting for a 20-day-high breakout before entering on the DI (against sideways losses): great in a simple simulator; with the real engine the DI alone improves (4.1 → 8.7), but the full system gets worse in training (9.2 → 7.4). Not applied.

Wave classification (impulse vs correction from subwaves, ADX and ATR) and fading when an indicator "team" says "end of wave": loses in every variant. It detects ends well (72 % vs 42 % base), but by the time it's confirmed it's too late.

Lower timeframes: the DI on 1h loses −1,088R in the exam because of costs. What works is a \~20-DAY breakout, on whatever candle (on 4h = 120 bars, on 8h = 60).

Shorts on stocks, gold and indices: they lose. RSI / EWO divergences as entries: nothing. Commodities (soy, wheat, cocoa, coffee, platinum, copper…): profitable in 2001–12, flat in 2013–26. Only gold holds up.

More coins: the full system on the top 20 or top 30 by volume instead of the top 10: the exam drops from 4.4 to 3.9 and to 1.1. More alts = more noise.

Tuning parameters by stock type (ETFs, low / mid / high volatility): overfitting (ETFs: 14.8 in training → 2.1 in the exam). One rule for all.

4. Current state

Bot v0.8 on demo: dynamic universe, core, monthly review. Order tests against a simulated exchange (failing stops, cut-off orders, BE, shorts) and a stop watchdog.

Stocks: daily paper scanner with the same monthly review.

Next (v0.9): the improved wave-3 start, bigger size after losing streaks, and gold / Nasdaq perps.

5. Questions

Losing streak → bigger size. Is this a known effect in trend systems or an artifact? How would you validate it better? I already have the random control and the train / exam split. Would you use it while lowering base risk to keep the drawdown the same?

A monthly review over 26 candidates is a form of "trying many things". What multiple-testing correction would you use? Does the rule (36 months, ratio ≥ 2, profitable in both halves) look reasonable?

Gold and indices on crypto perps (BingX, etc.): real experience with funding, spreads and weekend gaps?

Demo vs backtest: how many weeks or trades would you wait before going live, and what gap would make you stop?

Core losses in sideways markets are still the weak spot, and nothing that filters entries has helped. Ideas that aren't an entry filter?

Thanks again to everyone who commented last time: the liquidity universe and the cold start were the best criticism. The numbers went down, but now I believe them.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Dropping the numbers and showing the training and exam split is the right move, and it makes this much easier to trust. On the size-up after losses, I'd check that the extra gain isn't coming from a few big breakouts, and see if it holds coin by coin and year by year. Count every idea you've tried, not just the 26, as trials when you think about luck, and run the same monthly review on random strategies to see what it picks by chance. For going live, I'd write down before the demo starts how many trades you need and how big a gap from the backtest means stop. Cymetica's Backtest Labs can keep the last 30% of history aside as out-of-sample, which is a simple way to add one more clean test.

replies.author: lks777
replies.body: Good points. Two I haven't done and will: (1) run the same monthly review on random strategies to see what it selects by pure chance, and (2) write down before the demo how many trades I need and what gap vs backtest means stop. I'll post that rule before the demo starts so I can't move it later. For a clean holdout I already have the untouched coins 11–30, but I'll keep the "count every variant as a trial" idea in mind.

comments.author: spoidercide
comments.body:
Honestly, you've done more proper testing than most people posting strategies here. A few things I'd still check before going live:

Lookahead bias: Especially ZigZag and wave-3 signals. Make sure those swing points were actually known when the trades happened.

Fresh out-of-sample data: Once you've looked at the exam results and adjusted things, that period isn't really untouched anymore.

Multiple testing: You've tested way more than 26 strategies counting all the filters, exits, and variations. Look into Hansen SPA, PBO, and Deflated Sharpe Ratio.

Losing-streak sizing: Compare it against constant sizing at the same overall risk. A 55% increase in drawdown is pretty significant. I'd also bootstrap the results and check whether the effect survives across different coins and periods.

Portfolio correlation: Six profitable trend strategies might just be six versions of the same trade. Check how much each actually improves the portfolio.

Monte Carlo: Block-bootstrap the portfolio returns to preserve correlated losses. Look at worst-case drawdowns, not just the average outcome.

Execution: Historical futures aren't the same as BingX perps. Funding, spreads, slippage, weekend pricing, and stop failures need separate testing.

I'd also benchmark the whole thing against basic volatility-scaled trend following without the monthly selection process.

Biggest thing for me is the 2x sizing after losses. Interesting result, but I'd want much stronger evidence before risking actual SIZE on it.

Nobody says you have to allocate port to do a live run.

Just throw in whatever amount of money you're willing to gladly lose to fund your research.

Don't get emotional if it does well or does poorly, just collect data to try and get more of what you want and less of what you dont.

I'm really glad this isn't another person in an emotional rollercoaster over their paper trading ai agent.  
Those guys would pull the profit out early or panic stop the bot before it left drawdown for profit.  
Thats what happens if you have 0 real 1:1 knowledge you can see within code and parameters that stay consistent as to what the system your "agent" trades on.

This belongs more in r/algotrading good work.

replies.author: lks777
replies.body:
Thanks, this is exactly the kind of list I was hoping for. Where I stand on each:
Lookahead: pivots only count once the ZigZag has confirmed them, and the daily DI is rebuilt at each 8H close using only closed bars. I did catch one ZigZag bug earlier that inflated a result (67% → ~50% real), so I'll run a truncated-data check: replay bar by bar and make sure no signal changes when future bars are removed.
Contaminated OOS: agreed, the exam period isn't clean anymore. Two partial fixes so far: a "vault" of coins ranked 11–30 that were never used to pick anything (the system scored 0.7 there; only one new piece survived), and a cold start where I picked the portfolio with 2018–21 data only and let it run 2022–26. That came out roughly equal to the S&P with twice the drawdown. That's the number I trust most.
Multiple testing: fair hit. Each new piece passed a random control (same number of entries chosen at random, usually 0/30), but I haven't run SPA, PBO or the Deflated Sharpe on the whole search. Adding that.
2× after losses: I compared it at equal drawdown (×2 after 3 losses with base risk cut ÷1.44 → same drawdown, ~20% more gain), but you're right that it needs per-coin and per-year checks. It's not going into the next version, and definitely not with real size.
Correlation: pieces were added one at a time and each step was measured. I'll also do leave-one-out to see what each adds on its own.
Monte Carlo: I only did a monthly bootstrap so far, and I already saw it underestimates drawdowns because losses cluster. Block bootstrap is next. I'm sizing for 30R+, not the backtest drawdown.
Execution: costs are 0.3% round trip + 0.01%/8H funding, with per-coin costs from real order books. Signals come from Binance spot and execution is on BingX perps, which is exactly why it's running in demo first.
Vol-scaled baseline: I replicated the Donchian ensemble from the 2025 Zarattini et al. paper. In my universe it made +4.8%/yr, and only +0.5%/yr since 2022. I'll also compare against fixed pieces without the monthly selection.
And yes, live will be small money I'm fine losing, treated as research.
